title: Effect of dimensions of place attachment on residents' word-of-mouth behavior
authors: Ning (Chris) Chen, Larry Dwyer & Tracey Firth, 2014
research_question: To examine and compare the effect of residents' different dimensions of place attachment on their word-of-mouth (WOM) behavior in two cities: Sydney, Australia and Shanghai, China.
hypotheses: H1: The more satisfied residents are with the place, the more they identify with the place.
H1: The more satisfied residents are with the place, the more they depend on the place.
H1: The more satisfied residents are with the place, the more they are affectively connected to the place.
H1: The more satisfied residents are with the place, the stronger social bonds they commit to the place.
H1: There is a positive relationship between place satisfaction and place memory.
H1: There is a positive relationship between place satisfaction and place expectation.
H2: The more attached residents are to the place, the more they generate one-to-one WOM.

methodology.participant_demographics: 361 Sydney residents (mean age 40.5, 50.1% male, mean residence 24.4 years); 330 Shanghai residents (mean age 32.6, 48.5% male, mean residence 20.2 years). All participants had lived in their respective city for at least one year.
methodology.environment_setting: Urban residential (Sydney, Australia and Shanghai, China)
methodology.environmental_features: Not specific physical environmental features, but residents' psychological relationship with their city (place attachment dimensions).

measures.place_attachment: Six-dimensional construct: Place Identity, Place Dependence, Affective Attachment, Social Bonding (attitudinal); Place Memory, Place Expectation (interactional). Measured with 15 adapted items from Yuksel et al. (2009), Nielsen-Pincus et al. (2010), Kyle et al. (2005). Interactional dimensions were developed for this research.
measures.word_of_mouth: One-to-one WOM behavior, measured with a three-item, 7-point Likert scale adapted from Arnett, German, and Hunt (2003).
measures.place_satisfaction: Overall place satisfaction, measured with a three-item, 7-point Likert scale (1 'Very dissatisfied' to 7 'Very satisfied').

methodology.data_analysis: Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using IBM SPSS Amos 20. Maximum likelihood (ML) estimation.

limitations: The formation of place attachment is a very complicated process which usually takes a long time.
The study focused on one-to-one WOM; further research should examine other types of WOM behavior (one-to-many, many-to-many).
Future research should test the validity of the six-dimensional place attachment construct for short-term place relationships (e.g., for visitors or tourists).
Future research should investigate the possible factors contributing to the formation of place attachment and influencing place attachment on WOM, and why residents are satisfied/what they expect.
The model needs to be tested further by including respondents from different destinations and cultural backgrounds to study differences.
future_research: Test the validity of the six-dimensional place attachment construct to short-term place relationships, such as for visitors or tourists.
Understand the possible factors contributing to the formation of place attachment and influencing place attachment on WOM behavior.
Understand why residents are satisfied with and what they expect from the place.

Examine the association between place attachment and other types of WOM behavior, such as one-to-many and many-to-many, to determine their relative strengths and implications for destination marketing and management.
Test the model further by including respondents from different destinations and cultural backgrounds to study whether there are logical explanations for the differences in the model testing.
